chapter_title: What is Virginal; or, otherwise, what is Continent
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

** ¶3. ** What is called * virginal* belongs to the mystery of the infinite degrees of the Divine itself. It is called pure and untouched because it is that wisdom which has never undergone spiritual death , nor descended into conflict with the ass aults of evil and falsity. It ab ides in the Divine as it was given — whole , uncont aminated, knowing nothing of prof anation.

**¶4.** What is called *continent*, however , pert ains to the mystery of that wisdom which descended from the Divine and became inter mingled with fals ity. It was obsc ured and def iled within corporeal and sensual states of mind, and afterward was elevated back toward interior states. It is called self -restrained because it passed through contam ination and was recovered.

** ¶5.** Furthermore , those wis doms which remain in celest ial p urity — should they come forth against evil — do not undergo spiritual death, nor are they touched by prof anation. They are preserved in their original integrity.

**¶6.** On the other hand, what is called *continent* is that wisdom which became com mingled with falsity, was pur ified, was drawn upward out of all natural and sensual states of the created mind, and was established in the Divine . It is called self-restrained because it once t asted the concupiscence of self -love; but afterward it was cleansed of that love and became consecrated to what is holy .

**¶7.** What is called *virginal* is that wisdom which was purified through the manifest ation of the Divine Human in its medi ating form. It was elevated and att ained the inmost celestial states. It was confirmed in the very likeness of Divine good. Though it passed through the world , it was restored to innoc ence through the Lord 's appearing — and so is named pure , as though it had never been touched .

**¶8.** What is called *continent* is the remn ants of that wisdom which remained behind after the first purification. These remnants pass through successive states of vastation and reformation — descending into obsc urity, ascending again toward light . A portion of this wisdom enters the ultimate natural degree of the mind — the ou termost state of human thought and aff ection. And even there , in that natural state, it is chosen: it receives faith joined to charity, and becomes consecrated as holy . This is what is called self-restrained — wisdom that has known evil , passed through tem ptation, and by long combat been confirmed in good .

---

* A note on the two categories :* The entire passage distingu ishes between two modes by which Divine wisdom exists in created beings . The ** virginal** is wisdom preserved in celest ial innoc ence — either never having descended , or restored to innoc ence through the Lord's medi ating presence . The **continent** is wisdom that underwent the full circuit of the Fall — mixture with falsity, de filement in the sens ual mind , grad ual pur ification through temptation, and final reformation . Swedenborg's doctrine recogn izes both : the celest ial, who receive good directly and are preserved from prof anation, and the spiritual , who must be regener ated through combat with evil and the long labor of rep entance. Both are made holy — but by different paths .

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: What is called 'virginal' is assigned to the mystery of the aeons of greatness. And they called it 'virginal' by the category of all the light that did not [taste] of death, nor come to the enemy's war.

However, what is called 'continent' occurs to the mystery of the light that came and was mixed with the darkness. It was defiled in bodies [of flesh and in the creatures; it was cleansed] and went up to the light. [They] called [it 'co]ntinent'.
Furthermore, the holy vir[gin]als [that abide in the aeons of greatness,] should they come out against the en[emy to the war, they do not] taste death, nor [suffer defilement].

On the other hand, what is called 'continent' [is this li]ght that mixed with the darkness, was purif[ie]d, came [up f]rom all the creatures, and was confirmed in the great[ness]. They called it 'continent' since it tasted [of the l]ust; but afterwards was cleansed from it and [become an] holy one.
Furthermore, what is called ['vi]rginal' is this light that was purified by the ima[ge] of the [A]mbassador. It wen[t up and] attained [the] he[ights. It was] confirmed in the image of the gods.

Again, what is [called] 'continent' is the remainder of this light th[at] remained behind, from what was cleansed. It goes up and comes down in transmigration. Al[so], there is a part [of] it that shall come and attain the form of [hum]an [fl]esh. Again, that one too shall be chosen in the flesh, [accept] the hope, and become an holy one. And they name it 'continent'.

Furthermore, what is named 'virginal' is the Light Mind. However, on the other hand, what is called 'contin[ent]' is the new man, should it be purified from this old man. And it is cleansed and strips off the sin that is compounded with it, and it becomes a continent one.
